stem: A heavy nucleus at rest breaks into two parts A and B which fly off with velocities in the ratio 27 : 8. The ratio of radii B and A is (assumed spherical in shape)
solution:
Momentum is conserved: \(m_Av_A = m_Bv_B\), so \(\frac{m_A}{m_B} = \frac{v_B}{v_A} = \frac{8}{27}\).
Since \(R \propto A^{1/3} \propto m^{1/3}\): \(\frac{R_B}{R_A} = \left(\frac{27}{8}\right)^{1/3} = \frac{3}{2}\).
\(R_B : R_A = 3 : 2\).

stem: A radioactive nucleus of mass M emits a photon of frequency \(\nu\) and the nucleus recoils. The recoil energy will be
solution:
The photon carries momentum \(p = \frac{h\nu}{c}\); the nucleus recoils with the same momentum.
Recoil energy \(= \frac{p^2}{2M} = \frac{(h\nu)^2}{2Mc^2}\), which is option 4 (printed with lowercase m for the nucleus mass).
reasoning: Option 4 prints lowercase m in the denominator (the stem's mass is M); kept as printed. | Option 4 prints lowercase m in the denominator while the stem names the mass M; it is evidently the intended \(\frac{(h\nu)^2}{2Mc^2}\). Option 3 has the wrong dimensions.

\(= 216\,\text{MeV}\).

b) radius of nucleus is proportional to cube of mass number

solution:

Nuclear density is the same for all nuclei (a is correct) and the nuclear force is charge independent (c is correct).
The radius varies as \(R = R_0 A^{1/3}\): proportional to the cube ROOT of the mass number, not its cube, so b is wrong. Only a and c are correct.

stem: In a nuclear fission reaction of an isotope of mass M, three similar daughter nuclei of same mass are formed. The speed of a daughter nuclei in terms of mass defect \(\Delta M\) will be
solution:
Energy released \(\Delta M c^2\) goes into the kinetic energy of three daughters of mass about \(\frac{M}{3}\) each moving with speed v.
\(\Delta M c^2 = 3 \times \frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{M}{3}v^2 = \frac{1}{2}Mv^2\).
\(v = c\sqrt{\frac{2\Delta M}{M}}\).

subtopic: Size of nucleus, Mass defect, binding energy
stem:
Consider the following statements.
S1 : The nuclear force is independent of the charge of nucleons
S2 : The number of nucleons in the nucleus of an atom is equal to the number of electrons in the atom.
S3 : All nuclei have masses that are less than the sum of the masses of constituent nucleons.
Choose the correct statement (s)
solution:
S1 is true: the nuclear force is charge independent.
S2 is false: the nucleon number is A while the electron number equals Z.
S3 is true: every bound nucleus has a mass defect. So S1 and S3.
reasoning: Option 2 cites S4, which the stem does not list; as printed.

stem:
Which of the following are correct?
I. Nuclear density is a constant for all matter.
II. Nuclear density is around \(2.3 \times 10^{17}\,\text{Kg/m}^3\)
III. Nuclear density is very large compared to ordinary matter
IV. Mass of ordinary matter is mainly due to nucleus as nucleus carries almost all the mass of an atom that makes up the matter
solution:
Nuclear density is the same for all nuclei, about \(2.3 \times 10^{17}\,\text{kg/m}^3\), far larger than ordinary matter.
Almost all of an atom's mass is in its nucleus, so IV is also true. All four are correct.

\({}_{3}^{8}X \longrightarrow {}_{3}^{7}Y + n_{0}^{1}\) energy of neutron must be (assume all energy released in the reaction to be carried by neutron)
solution:
BE of X \(= 8 \times 6.00 = 48\,\text{MeV}\); BE of Y \(= 7 \times 8.00 = 56\,\text{MeV}\); a free neutron has zero BE.
\(Q = 56 - 48 = 8.00\,\text{MeV}\), all carried by the neutron.

solution:

Fraction of KE retained \(= \left(\frac{v'}{v}\right)^2 = \left[\frac{A - 1}{A + 1}\right]^2\).

stem: Choose the only correct statement.
options: In a stable nucleus, the number of neutrons > the number of protons
Nuclei with atomic number greater than 82 show a tendency to fuse
A stable nucleus, in general has even number of protons and odd number of neutrons
The proton-proton nuclear force > proton-neutron nuclear force > neutron - neutron nuclear force.
solution:
Option 2 is wrong: nuclei with \(Z > 82\) tend to break up, not fuse. Option 3 is wrong: stable nuclei are mostly even-even. Option 4 is wrong: the nuclear force is charge independent.
Option 1 holds in general: beyond the lightest nuclei, stable nuclei have more neutrons than protons.

stem: Choose the incorrect statement.

solution:
One \(\alpha\) then two \(\beta^{-}\) restores Z with A lower by 4: an isotope (true). \(\gamma\) emission leaves a nucleus of the same Z and A in a different energy state: an isomer (true). Nuclear forces are charge independent (true).
Nuclear forces are non-central (they have a tensor part), so statement 4 is incorrect.

| C) | \({}_{43}^{97}\text{Te} \rightarrow {}_{42}^{97}\text{Mo} + e^{+} + \nu\) | 3. | \(\beta^{-}\) - decay |
| D) | \({}_{54}^{120}\text{Xe} + e^{-} \rightarrow {}_{53}^{120}\text{I} + \nu\) | 4. | \(\alpha\) - decay |
solution:
A emits \({}_{2}^{4}\text{He}\): \(\alpha\) decay (4). B emits \(e^{-}\) and \(\bar{\nu}\): \(\beta^{-}\) decay (3).

stem: In a nuclear reactor energy released per fission of \(U^{235}\) nucleus is 200 MeV. Find the number of fissions per second required to release 1 kilowatt power (nearly)

Energy per fission \(= 200 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-13} = 3.2 \times 10^{-11}\,\text{J}\).

stem:
**Assertion:** If a heavy nucleus is split into two lighter nuclei each nuclei will have more binding energy per nucleon than original nucleus.
**Reason:** When heavy nucleus splits into lighter nucleus it becomes stable.
options: Both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
Both assertion and reason are true and reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
Assertion is true but reason is false
Assertion is false but reason is true
solution:
The middle-mass fragments lie nearer the peak of the binding energy curve, so each has a higher binding energy per nucleon than the heavy parent.
Higher binding energy per nucleon is what makes the products more stable, so both are true and the reason explains the assertion.
reasoning: The reason states a consequence (greater stability) rather than a cause; some keys treat it as not explaining the assertion. Taken here as the correct explanation.
